_readme: Normally you manage this from Settings > AI models in the app: add a provider, then tick
the models you want. This file is what those screens edit, and you can edit it by hand too.
It is re-read whenever it changes - no server restart needed.
"chain" is the list of models offered in the chat. On Auto it is tried top to bottom: a model
that hits a rate limit is put on cooldown and skipped, and is used again as soon as it recovers.
API keys are never stored here. Each provider names a variable (key_env) that lives in
backend/.env; one variable may hold several keys separated by commas.
Provider options: name, base_url, key_env, free (all | none | auto), free_tier (note shown in
Settings), signup_url, daily_reset_utc_hour, max_input_chars, headers. Providers Zyqra knows
(see app/ai/presets.py) inherit their defaults; "custom": true marks one you added by URL.
Model options: provider, model (exact API id), label, enabled (false switches it off),
free (true/false overrides the Free / Paid label), max_input_chars.
settings.free_only: true means models that are billed are never called.

gemini.name: Google Gemini
gemini.free_tier: Free, no card. Limits are per model and shown in AI Studio; daily quota resets at midnight Pacific.

groq.name: Groq
groq.free_tier: Free, no card. About 30 requests/min and 1,000 requests/day per model; very fast.

nvidia.name: NVIDIA NIM
nvidia.free_tier: Free endpoints, about 40 requests/min. Meant for prototyping.

mistral.name: Mistral AI
mistral.free_tier: Free plan, no card. Monthly free allowance; exact limits are shown in the Mistral console.

openrouter.name: OpenRouter
openrouter.free_tier: Models ending in :free. 20 requests/min and 50 requests/day (1,000/day after a one-time $10 top-up).

cloudflare.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
cloudflare.free_tier: 10,000 Neurons/day shared across models, resets 00:00 UTC. Needs CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID too.
